note: The v3 return is the pre-panel automated quality check, not a panel: the one blocking row is `solvable` (the reference solution and the 12-hour estimate are an unreasonable amount of work for an expert, beyond a few hours). The returned artifact is byte-identical to rev1 (its digest equals the v2 ledger returned_snapshot_sha256); rev2, which answered the 34 v2 panel findings, was never judged. The same rev1 snapshot passed the solvable check in evaluations 1-3.

findings.rationale: the finding is about the amount of work, which is real: the reference was 1,375 lines with a 12-hour estimate. Backed by cutting breadth and keeping the hard thing: l, y, pattern back-references, I/M, numeric/control escapes, case conversion and equivalence classes are dropped together with their tests, prose and wrong paths (7 removed obligations); leftmost-longest matching, every address form, the cycle rules and -s stay. The reference is now 1,060 lines with an honest 5-hour estimate, and the trimmed roster of 704 cases equals GNU sed 4.9 on every case.

gate.rule: task.toml:expert-hours-bound (scripts/task-policy.py, advisory: warns above 8 expert hours; --strict preflight promotes it to FAIL), with scripts/tests/test_task_policy.py::ExpertHoursBoundTests

previous_findings.response: answered in rev2 (workspace/reports/tbrain-gnu-sed-reimplementation/rev2-tree-archive/revision-ledger.json); rev2 was never judged by the platform because the 04:14Z upload carried the rev1 bytes. The rev2 repairs that concern retained features (multi-line a/i/c escapes, [:xdigit:], tab before a command, backslash delimiter, escaped delimiter in the replacement, ERE \? literal, D keeping the t flag, the audit-hook enforcement) are carried into rev3; the repairs that concerned dropped features (y numeric escapes, fixed-width numeric escapes, I with back-references, case conversion across an empty group, M mode) fall away with their promises.
